input.content: Pattern: "simplification" that drops an ownership/equality guard before an unconditional delete/pop causes a stale or superseding operation to clobber newer state. Concrete case (cleanup.py cleanup_setup): store.active is keyed by workspace_id and records the owning setup_id. Original guarded `if association["setup_id"] == setup_id: store.active.pop(workspace_id)`. Removing the guard makes a late/duplicate cleanup for an OLD setup_id delete the active connection established by a NEWER completed setup for the same workspace → active_connection() silently returns None. Lesson: a delete keyed by one identifier (workspace_id) while the caller's intent is scoped to another (setup_id) must verify ownership before removing; a passing test that only cleans up its own setup does not cover the superseding-setup case. Severity P1 (silent loss of valid state, recoverable).
